title: Chapter 6 Mastery Quiz: Gestalt Psychology & The Humanistic Movement
description: Demonstrate comprehensive mastery of Gestalt laws, Köhler's insight, Lewin's field theory, Carl Rogers, and Maslow's hierarchy.

questions.question: What does the German word 'Gestalt' most closely translate to in English?
questions.explanation: Gestalt means whole, shape, unified pattern, or configuration.

questions.question: Which trio of psychologists founded the Gestalt school in Germany in the early 20th century?

options.text: Max Wertheimer, Kurt Koffka, and Wolfgang Köhler
Wilhelm Wundt, Edward Titchener, and G. Stanley Hall
Sigmund Freud, Carl Jung, and Alfred Adler
John Watson, B.F. Skinner, and Edward Thorndike

questions.explanation: Wertheimer, Koffka, and Köhler were the three co-founders of the Gestalt psychology movement.

questions.question: What is the precise statement of the Gestalt principle regarding wholes and parts?

options.text: The whole is other than the sum of its parts
The whole is equal to the sum of sensory atoms
The parts are more important than the whole
Wholes do not exist in reality

questions.explanation: Kurt Koffka explicitly corrected the mistranslation: Gestalt theory holds that the whole is 'other' (different in kind) than the sum of its parts.

questions.question: Which Gestalt law explains why you see rows of circles and rows of squares rather than mixed random columns?
questions.explanation: The Law of Similarity states that visually similar elements are automatically grouped together into units.

questions.question: When you look at an incomplete circle with a small gap and automatically perceive a whole circle, which Gestalt law is at work?
questions.explanation: The Law of Closure states that the visual system fills in missing contour information to complete recognizable shapes.

questions.question: What overarching Gestalt principle (Law of Prägnanz) asserts that visual stimuli are organized into the simplest, most regular, and harmonious configuration possible?

options.text: The Law of Good Figure (Simplicity / Prägnanz)

questions.explanation: Prägnanz (good figure / simplicity) is the central Gestalt law: the perceptual field organizes into the simplest possible structure.

questions.question: In his chimpanzee research on Tenerife, what did Wolfgang Köhler observe that directly contradicted Thorndike's trial-and-error model?

options.text: Sultan solved the two-stick problem suddenly through insightful mental restructuring of the tools
Apes required thousands of food pellets before learning anything
Conditioning was faster when using electric shocks

questions.explanation: Köhler showed that chimpanzees display sudden insight learning (Einsicht)—grasping the relational whole of the problem and tool.

questions.question: What famous formula did Kurt Lewin formulate to express that behavior is determined by the person interacting with their psychological environment?
questions.explanation: Lewin's formula B = f(P, E) states that Behavior is a function of the Person and their subjective Environment.

questions.question: What psychological phenomenon discovered by Bluma Zeigarnik demonstrates that uncompleted tasks are recalled significantly better than completed ones?
questions.explanation: The Zeigarnik Effect demonstrates that unresolved goals maintain cognitive tension in memory until completed.

questions.question: Why did Kurt Lewin's research on leadership styles (Autocratic, Democratic, and Laissez-faire) have such a profound historical impact?

options.text: It empirically demonstrated that democratic leadership produced higher satisfaction and creative cooperation than authoritarian control
It showed that leaders should never communicate with subordinates
It proved that only monarchy works in organizations
It proved that leadership is 100% genetically determined

questions.explanation: Lewin showed that group climates experimentally shape individual behavior, providing empirical support for democratic leadership.

questions.question: What nickname did Humanistic psychology adopt to distinguish itself from Psychoanalysis and Behaviorism?
questions.explanation: Humanistic psychology designated itself the 'Third Force' behind Psychoanalysis and Behaviorism.

questions.question: Carl Rogers replaced the traditional clinical term 'patient' with what word, signaling equality and agency in therapy?
questions.explanation: Rogers intentionally used 'client' to abandon medicalized hierarchy and emphasize the individual's self-directing autonomy.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of Carl Rogers's three necessary and sufficient conditions for therapeutic personality change?
questions.explanation: Rogers's three core therapeutic conditions are Congruence, Unconditional Positive Regard, and Empathy.

questions.question: What did Carl Rogers define as 'Unconditional Positive Regard'?

options.text: Complete, non-judgmental acceptance and valuing of the client without strings attached
Blindly agreeing with every action the client takes, even criminal acts
Providing food rewards every time the client arrives on time

questions.explanation: Unconditional Positive Regard is warm, non-possessive caring and acceptance of the client as a human being of inherent worth.

questions.question: According to Carl Rogers, what causes psychological distress and neurosis in an individual?

options.text: Incongruence between the Real Self and the Ideal Self forced by conditions of worth
Lack of physical punishment in childhood
Failure to record dreams in childhood

questions.explanation: Rogers posited that when individuals internalize conditions of worth, a painful gap opens between their real self and ideal self.

questions.question: What is at the very base of Abraham Maslow's original Hierarchy of Needs?
questions.explanation: Physiological needs (survival needs: food, water, air, sleep) form the fundamental foundation of Maslow's pyramid.

questions.question: What need sits at the apex of Maslow's hierarchy, representing the realization of one's full personal potential?
questions.explanation: Self-Actualization is the desire to fulfill one's creative, intellectual, and human potential ('What a man can be, he must be').

questions.question: In Maslow's theory, how do 'Deficiency Needs' (D-Needs) differ from 'Being/Growth Needs' (B-Needs)?

options.text: D-needs arise from physical or social deprivation; B-needs arise from the innate desire to grow and flourish
D-needs occur only in animals; B-needs occur in humans
D-needs are pleasant; B-needs are always painful

questions.explanation: D-needs (hunger, safety, belonging) stem from deficit; B-needs (self-actualization, truth, beauty) stem from growth.

questions.question: What term did Abraham Maslow give to transcendent, profound moments of awe, unity, and bliss experienced during self-actualization?
questions.explanation: Maslow described 'peak experiences' as rare, ecstatic moments of universal clarity, harmony, and joy.

questions.question: What modern subfield of psychology, founded in the late 1990s by Martin Seligman, is the direct scientific heir to humanistic psychology?
questions.explanation: Positive Psychology adopted Humanism's emphasis on human strengths, flourishing, and well-being, while applying rigorous quantitative empirical methods.

questions.question: What is the primary scientific critique commonly leveled against Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs?

options.text: Empirical studies show that human motivation does not follow a strict, rigid hierarchical order (e.g. starving artists still create masterpieces)
It was completely rejected by business and educational leaders
It was stolen from Ivan Pavlov

questions.explanation: Research shows needs do not always follow a rigid stepwise hierarchy—humans frequently pursue esteem, love, or art despite deprivation of lower needs.

questions.question: What shared conviction united Gestalt psychology and Humanistic psychology against behaviorism?

options.text: Both insisted that human experience must be understood as an indivisible, meaningful whole rather than dissected into mechanical pieces
Both believed all mental life is an illusion
Both argued that humans have no free will

questions.explanation: Both movements championed holism against reductionism: Gestalt in perception and cognition, Humanism in personality and therapy.
